name: NETSCOUT AED — Surge in High-Confidence Threat Activity Against a Bank Internet Service
description:
Attacker objective
Compromise an internet-facing banking service through a coordinated exploitation or botnet campaign — many distinct high-reputation threat sources (active exploiters, botnet C2, named exploit tooling) targeting the same service in a short window.

Attack logic
The edge appliance blocks inbound traffic from sources flagged by threat intelligence as active exploiters, botnet command-and-control, or named exploit campaigns. A surge in the number of distinct such sources targeting one protected service — well above the steady background of internet scanning — indicates a coordinated, targeted campaign against that service.

Why this detection works
Counting distinct high-confidence threat sources per protected service over a short window separates a coordinated campaign from the constant low background of individual scanners the appliance blocks.

False positives
A general internet-wide scanning wave or botnet sweep that incidentally raises counts across many services (not targeted); a threat-intel feed false-positive.

Tuning
Set the distinct-source surge threshold above the observed background; prioritise surges against internet-banking and webmail services; correlate with F5 WAF attack volume against the same service.

Required telemetry
NETSCOUT Arbor Edge Defense (CEF): Threat Name (deviceCustomString6), Threat Category (cs7), Protection Group (deviceCustomString2), source.ip (external threat source), destination.ip (bank service).
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. deviceCustomString2 = the targeted service; review the threat names/categories and the distinct source IPs and their geography/ASN.
2. A surge of exploiter/C2 sources against internet banking or webmail can precede a real intrusion attempt — raise monitoring and correlate with F5 WAF and FortiGate/PAN-OS for the same service.
3. Confirm whether any of the campaign traffic was not blocked (reached the app).
false_positives: A general internet-wide scanning wave or botnet sweep that incidentally raises counts across many services (not targeted); a threat-intel feed false-positive.
query: observer.vendor:"NETSCOUT" and (cef.extensions.deviceCustomString6:("Botnet Command and Control" or "Active Exploiters" or "MOVEit Transfer" or "CnC Other" or "Eleven11 Botnet" or "DNS Flood") or cef.extensions.cs7:"Command and Control")
